title: An okay laptop with 16GB of RAM is better than a nice laptop with 8GB, and this $520 HP OmniBook proves it
summary: Laptop prices are out of whack. $500 used to get you a tolerable laptop, and $900 got you a really good one. They often had similar CPU, RAM, and storage options because that stuff was comparatively cheap; the difference was often in build quality and screen rather than power. But RAMageddon has thrown everything off. […]
llm_summary: Even modest‑priced laptops can now outperform pricier models because RAM has become the biggest performance bottleneck. A used HP OmniBook with 16 GB of RAM and a modest CPU feels faster and more responsive than a newer, better‑built laptop that only has 8 GB, showing that memory capacity now matters more than chassis quality or screen specs.
